## Catchment overview {#sec-jeksla-overview}

Jeksla is a small tributary of Leira with a catchment area of just 17 km². Land cover is dominated by agriculture (39 %), forest (38 %) and urban areas (22 %). See @fig-jeksla and @tbl-jeksla-land-cover. More than 90 % of the catchment is below the marine limit and 46 % of the land area is underlain by marine deposits. The catchment is therefore classified as *leirpåvirket* (clay-influenced) and the *Good/Moderate* threshold for TOTP is set to 80 μg-P/l (@fig-marine-clay and @tbl-leir-totp-bounds).

![Maps of the Jeksla catchment. Left: Land cover based NIBIO's AR50 dataset. Right: Point source discharges from industry and municipal wastewater plants (≥50 p.e.).](./plots/jeksla.png){#fig-jeksla width=500 fig-align="center"}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-jeksla-land-cover
#| tbl-cap: "Land cover proportions for Jeksla based on NIBIO's AR50 dataset."
#| echo: false

import pandas as pd

catch = "Jeksla"

# Read land cover data
df = pd.read_excel(r"./data/catchment_land_cover.xlsx")
df = df.set_index("klasse")

# Create total row
total = df.sum(numeric_only=True)
total.name = "Totalt"
df = pd.concat([df, total.to_frame().T])

# Convert to MultiIndex
new_cols = []
for col in df.columns:
    catchment, statistic = col.rsplit("_", 1)
    if statistic == "km2":
        statistic = "km²"
    elif statistic == "pct":
        statistic = "%"
    new_cols.append((catchment, statistic))
df.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples(new_cols, names=["Nedbørfelt", "AR50 klasse"])

# Select catchment
df = df[[catch]]

# Format
km2_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c[1] == "km²"]
pct_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c[1] == "%"]
for col in pct_cols:
    df[col] = df[col].round().astype(int)
fmt = {c: "{:.1f}" for c in km2_cols}

# Style
df.style.format(fmt).set_table_styles(
    [
        {"selector": "th.col_heading", "props": [("text-align", "center")]},
        {"selector": "th.col_heading.level0", "props": [("text-align", "center")]},
        {"selector": "th.col_heading.level1", "props": [("text-align", "center")]},
    ]
).map(lambda _: "font-weight: bold;", subset=pd.IndexSlice[["Totalt"], :])
```

There are no municipal wastewater treatment plants or industrial discharges within the Jeksla catchment. However, the catchment does receive wastewater discharges from spredt avløp and from rainwater and emergency overflows. Since most of the catchment lies within Lillestrøm kommune, the Lillestrøm-specific dataset of wastewater overflows (@sec-lillestrom-data) should provide a reasonably complete picture of overflows from the municipal sewerage network.

## Monitoring data {#sec-jeksla-monitoring}

The best monitoring data for Jeksla come from Vannmiljø station `002-30593` (Jeksla ved Haugli), which is located approximately 1.5 km upstream of the confluence with Leira (@fig-jeksla). The station has been monitored since 1998.

@fig-jeksla-ann-concs shows trends in mean annual concentrations estimated from the combined dataset for waterbody `002-599-R`. There are no significant trends for any parameters and nutrient concentrations are generally high. For TOTN, mean annual concentrations are typically 2000 to 4000 μg-N/l, which corresponds to *Bad* status under the Water Framework Directive. TOTP concentrations in recent years vary between about 60 and 125 μg-P/l and are generally above the *Good* status threshold of 80 μg-P/l.

![Trends in annual mean concentrations for waterbody `002-599-R` (Jeksla). Solid red lines show statistically significant linear trends ($p ≤ 0.05$); dashed red lines indicate weak evidence of a linear trend ($0.05 < p ≤ 0.10$); and dashed black lines indicate no statistically significant trend ($p > 0.10$). Background colours show thresholds for water quality status defined under the Water Framework Directive and taken from Vann-Nett, where available (*bad*, *poor*, *moderate*, *good* and *high*).](./plots/concs/ann_trends_waterbodies_002-599-R.png){#fig-jeksla-ann-concs width=800 fig-align="center"}

## Source apportionment {#sec-jeksla-sources}

@fig-teotil3-jeksla shows nutrient fluxes for Jeksla estimated from observed data (black lines) together with source-apportioned fluxes simulated by TEOTIL3 (stacked bars). Because the Jeksla catchment is small (17 km²) and occupies only part of a single REGINE unit, it is not possible to simulate nutrient fluxes explicitly using TEOTIL3 (see @sec-spatial-res for details). TEOTIL3's estimates of diffuse nutrient fluxes for Jeksla are therefore based on simulations from a wider area, scaled to match the size of the Jeksla catchment. **TEOTIL3 results for Jeksla are therefore approximate and must be interpreted with caution**, since they assume average land management for REGINE `002.CAA0`, rather than using Jeksla-specific data. Point inputs to Jeksla are represented explicitly, however, since these can be assigned to specific co-ordinates.

Based on available monitoring data, typical nutrient fluxes for Jeksla (waterbody `002-599-R`) are approximately:

 * 15 to 30 tonnes/year for TOTN
 * 0.5 to 1.5 tonnes/year for TOTP
 * 75 to 125 tonnes/year for TOC
 * 400 to 1200 tonnes/year for SS

![Annual nutrient fluxes for waterbody `002-599-R` (Jeksla). Black lines show fluxes estimated from monitoring data; stacked bars show source-apportioned fluxes simulated by TEOTIL3. TEOTIL3 results are approximate (see text).](./plots/modelled/mod_vs_obs_default_Jeksla_waterbody_002-599-R.png){#fig-teotil3-jeksla width=800 fig-align="center"}

@fig-jeksla-src-app shows the mean contribution of each source to annual fluxes during the period 2020 to 2024. As noted above, source apportionment for diffuse sources is based on data from a wider area, so results are approximate. According to TEOTIL3, agriculture is the main source of TOTN, TOTP and SS reaching the catchment outflow, while background areas, such as forest, contribute most of the TOC. These results are plausible based on the land cover map and the fact that the catchment does not include any major outlets from municipal wastewater or industrial plants. 

Wastewater discharges are estimated to provide 2.5 % of the TOTN flux, of which 1.5 % comes from spredt avløp and 1 % from rainwater and emergency overflows. For TOTP, spredt avløp contributes 2.5 % and wastewater overflows 1.5 %, making the total wastewater contribution for TOTP about 4 %. Urban areas, most notably the settlements at Kløfta and Lindeberg, also make a significant contribution: roughly 10 % for TOTN, TOTP & TOC, and 6 % for SS.

![Mean source-apportionment for waterbody `002-599-R` (Jeksla) based on TEOTIL3 simulations from 2020 to 2024. For clarity, labels are omitted for sources contributing less than 3 %. Results are approximate (see text)](./plots/modelled/src_app_default_Jeksla_waterbody_002-599-R.png){#fig-jeksla-src-app width=800 fig-align="center"}

## Load reductions and scenarios {#sec-jeksla-avlast}

During the decade from 2015 to 2024, the median annual flow volume at Jeksla ved Haugli (Vannmiljø station `002-30593`) was 6.5 Mm³/year. Taking the maximum concentrations for GES of 775 μg/l for N and 80 μg/l for P, the maximum annual load for *Good* status in a typical year is approximately 5 tonnes for TOTN and 0.5 tonnes for TOTP. Measured loads are almost always higher than this, and for TOTN measured fluxes are often too large by a factor of three to four (@fig-teotil3-jeksla).

@fig-jeksla-avlast shows distributions of annual avlastningsbehov estimated for each year between 2015 and 2024. Red curves show distributions based on measured loads, while blue curves are based on model output from TEOTIL3, which must be interpreted with caution. Distributions for TOTN are sharp and narrow, indicating the avlastningsbehov is well-defined. Based on monitoring data, the median avlastningsbehov for GES for TOTN is 64 %, and almost always between 60 % and 70 %. For TOTP, the distribution based on monitoring is much broader, reflecting greater interannual variability in measured fluxes. The median avlastningsbehov for TOTP using observed data is 20 %, but for some years it is as high as 70 %.  

![Distributions of annual avlastningsbehovene (in percent) for the ten year period from 2015 to 2024 based on observed fluxes (red curves) and fluxes simulated by TEOTIL3 (blue curves). Vertical dashed lines show the median avlastningsbehov based on each dataset i.e. the load reduction that would have achieved GES in roughly half of the ten year period.](./plots/modelled/avlast_Jeksla_waterbody_002-599-R.png){#fig-jeksla-avlast width=800 fig-align="center"}

@fig-leira-scens shows load reductions achieved in the Jeksla catchment under two management scenarios modelled by [Wallhead *et al.* (2026)](https://www.miljodirektoratet.no/publikasjoner/2026/april-2026/modellering-av-oslofjorden-scenarier-med-redusert-menneskelig-belastning-for-a-oppna-god-okologisk-tilstand/). As described above, the estimated reductions are derived from modelled changes across a larger area that includes the Jeksla catchment, rather than from measures implemented specifically within the catchment itself. The scenarios comprise packages of agricultural mitigation measures together with upgrades to municipal wastewater treatment plants (@sec-teo-scens).

Since there are no municipal wastewater treatment plants located within the Jeksla catchment, the scenario results do not show any reductions in wastewater discharges. However, the Lillestrøm-specific dataset of rainwater and emergency wastewater overflows suggests that additional reductions of 1 % for TOTN and 1.5 % for TOTP could be achieved if overflows from Lillestrøm kommune were reduced to zero (@sec-jeksla-sources).

For agriculture, NIBIO's results for scenario A indicate load reductions of 2 % for TOTN, 43 % for TOTP and 67 % for SS. In scenario B these reductions increase to 28 % for TOTN, 55 % for TOTP and 72 % for SS. Both scenarios comfortably achieve the median load reduction target of 20 % calculated for TOTP (black vertical line on @fig-jeksla-avlast), but neither scenario comes close to the median avlastningsbehov of 64 % for TOTN. Given the high nitrogen concentrations measured in the catchment, and the limited potential for load reductions at point sources, it seems unlikely that GES for TOTN can be achieved for Jeksla.

A summary of avlastningsbehovene for GES in Jeksla and the reductions achieved by scenarios A and B is shown in @tbl-scen_summary-jeksla.

![Load reductions achieved in the Jeksla catchment by scenarios A and B of [Wallhead *et al.* (2026)](https://www.miljodirektoratet.no/publikasjoner/2026/april-2026/modellering-av-oslofjorden-scenarier-med-redusert-menneskelig-belastning-for-a-oppna-god-okologisk-tilstand/). Black vertical lines on the plots for TOTN and TOTP show the median avlastningsbehov for GES estimated using observed data (@fig-jeksla-avlast).](./plots/modelled/oslomod_scens_Jeksla.png){#fig-jeksla-scens width=800 fig-align="center"}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scen_summary-jeksla
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of avlastningsbehov and scenario results for Jeksla."
#| echo: false

import pandas as pd

catch = "Jeksla"

# Read site data
xl_path = r"./data/scenario_summary.xlsx"
df = pd.read_excel(xl_path).query("`Nedbørfelt` == @catch")

wfd_col_dict = {
    "High": "#5893A9",
    "Good": "#6FB22C",
    "Moderate": "#FFF6A6",
    "Poor": "#F6A800",
    "Bad": "#E63D5C",
}


def color_wfd(val):
    color = wfd_col_dict.get(val)
    if not color:
        return ""

    text_color = "white" if val in ["Poor", "Bad"] else "black"
    return f"background-color: {color}; color: black;"


# Format
txt_cols = ["Nedbørfelt", "Vannforekomst ID", "Parameter", "Vann-Nett tilstand"]
num_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c not in txt_cols]
df[num_cols] = df[num_cols].round().astype("Int64")

# Style
(
    df.style.hide(axis="index")
    .format(na_rep="")
    .map(color_wfd, subset=["Vann-Nett tilstand"])
    .set_table_styles(
        [{"selector": "th.col_heading", "props": [("text-align", "center")]}]
    )
    .set_properties(subset=txt_cols, **{"text-align": "center"})
    .set_properties(subset=num_cols, **{"text-align": "right"})
)
```
